title: Describe Traditional Small Sort vs Belted ACB Bagging Flow (Shoot-to-Bag-to-Takeaway)
summary: Use the source-described process to explain how parcels move from sorter destinations into bags and onto takeaway belts in both a traditional small sort model and a belted ACB model, including the named operator actions (close destination/print/apply label/zips/reopen chute) versus the belted conveyor “slug” movement (bin dropped to takeaway conveyor → chute → bag station).
when_to_use: When you need to accurately communicate the difference between (1) traditional small sort bagging and (2) belted ACB bagging flow, using the source’s named elements: destination/shoot, bag, label, zipping, takeaway belt, chute reopening, and (for belted) bin dropped to takeaway conveyor as a slug down a chute into a bag station.
not_for: Do not use this as an operational troubleshooting procedure for live RMS/WCS/SSMS/robot systems, because the source provides a conceptual process description rather than live UI/DB/API steps.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Restate the two bagging flows using the source’s named sequence elements (traditional: close destination/print/apply label/zips/reopen chute; belted: bin dropped to takeaway conveyor as a slug → chute → bag station).

access_required: Access to the training video segment transcript/slide text for “What is OptiSweep Traditional vs Fortna's Solution” (segment_id: training_video_day1_segment_0004).

visual_references.description: Training video frame/slide showing the source-described Traditional small sort vs Belted ACB bagging flow steps and labels (destination/shoot → bag → takeaway belt; and belted: bin dropped to takeaway conveyor as a slug → chute → bag station).

steps.title: Identify the traditional small sort model described in the source
steps.purpose: Establish the correct traditional small sort sequence elements (destinations/shoot → bag → operator actions → takeaway belt → reopen chute) before comparing to the belted ACB model.
steps.instruction: From the source segment “What is OptiSweep Traditional vs Fortna's Solution” (training_video_day1_segment_0004), identify the traditional small sort elements: operators assigned sections of destinations (20-25) on a sorter; parcels divert down the destination and fall into a bag.
steps.expected_result: You can name the traditional small sort starting point and ownership: operators assigned sections of destinations (20-25) on a sorter, and parcels divert down the destination into a bag.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation includes the named traditional elements “operators are assigned sections of destinations (20-25) on a sorter” and “parcels divert down the destination and fall into a bag.”
steps.failure_condition: You cannot correctly distinguish the traditional starting elements (destination/shoot into a bag) from the belted model’s “bin dropped on a takeaway conveyor as a slug.”

actions.label: Review traditional flow description
actions.exact_action: Use the source segment text that states: “Operators are assigned sections of destinations (20-25) on a sorter. Parcels divert down the destination and fall into a bag.”

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot map the described elements to the traditional model (destination/shoot → bag), stop and re-check the source wording for “operators assigned sections of destinations (20-25),” “parcels divert down the destination,” and “fall into a bag.”

source_evidence.quote_or_evidence: “Operators are assigned sections of destinations (20-25) on a sorter. Parcels divert down the destination and fall into a bag.”

steps.title: Follow the traditional small sort sequence when a bag becomes full
steps.purpose: Capture the complete traditional bag-full operator action sequence and the final chute reopening step.
steps.instruction: Using the same source segment, follow the traditional bag-full sequence exactly as described: close the destination, print a label, apply the label to the bag, zip up the bag, place the bag on a takeaway belt, then reopen the chute.
steps.expected_result: You can restate the full traditional bag-full sequence with all named actions in order: close destination → prints label → applies label → zips up → places on takeaway belt → reopens chute.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation includes all named steps: “closes the destination, prints a label, applies the label to the bag, zips up the bag, places the bag on a takeaway belt, and then reopens the chute.”
steps.failure_condition: Your explanation omits one of the named actions (close/print/apply label/zip/place on takeaway belt/reopen chute) or substitutes belted ACB elements (bin dropped as a slug).

actions.label: Restate bag-full operator sequence
actions.exact_action: Restate the source sequence: “When the bag becomes full an operator closes the destination, prints a label, applies the label to the bag, zips up the bag, places the bag on a takeaway belt, and then reopens the chute.”

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot restate the traditional bag-full sequence with the named actions (close destination/print/apply label/zips/place on takeaway belt/reopen chute), stop and re-check the source wording for those exact elements.

source_evidence.quote_or_evidence: “When the bag becomes full an operator closes the destination, prints a label, applies the label to the bag, zips up the bag, places the bag on a takeaway belt, and then reopens the chute.”

steps.title: Identify the belted ACB model described in the source
steps.purpose: Establish the belted ACB starting mechanism (full destination bin dropped to takeaway conveyor as a slug) before describing the bag station actions.
steps.instruction: Using the source segment, identify the belted ACB mechanism: when a destination is full, the bin is dropped on a takeaway conveyor that conveys packages as a slug down a chute into a bag station.
steps.expected_result: You can name the belted ACB mechanism: full destination bin dropped onto takeaway conveyor → conveys packages as a slug down a chute → into a bag station.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation includes the named belted elements “bin is dropped on a takeaway conveyor,” “conveys the packages as a slug,” “go down a chute,” and “into a bag station.”
steps.failure_condition: You describe belted ACB using traditional operator destination close/print/apply/zip/reopen chute steps instead of the bin-drop + slug conveyor + chute + bag station mechanism.

actions.label: Review belted flow description
actions.exact_action: Use the source segment text that states: “In a Belted ACB solution when a destination is full the bin is dropped on a takeaway conveyor that conveys the packages as a slug that go down a chute into a bag station …”

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot map the described elements to the belted model (bin dropped to takeaway conveyor as a slug → chute → bag station), stop and re-check the source wording for “bin dropped,” “takeaway conveyor,” “slug,” “chute,” and “bag station.”

source_evidence.quote_or_evidence: “In a Belted ACB solution when a destination is full the bin is dropped on a takeaway conveyor that conveys the packages as a slug that go down a chute into a bag station …”

steps.title: Follow the belted ACB sequence at the bag station
steps.purpose: Complete the belted ACB flow by capturing the bag station user actions (label, zip, place on takeaway belt).
steps.instruction: Using the source segment, follow the bag station actions for belted ACB: user applies a label, zips up the bag, and places it on a takeaway belt.
steps.expected_result: You can restate the belted bag station actions: apply label → zip up bag → place on a takeaway belt.
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation includes the named bag station actions: “user applies a label, zips up the bag and places it on a takeaway belt.”
steps.failure_condition: Your explanation incorrectly includes traditional destination close/reopen chute steps for the belted model.

actions.label: Restate bag station actions
actions.exact_action: Restate the source sequence: “...where the user applies a label, zips up the bag and places it ona takeaway belt.”

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot restate the belted bag station actions with the named steps (apply label/zip/place on takeaway belt), stop and re-check the source wording for those exact elements.

source_evidence.quote_or_evidence: “...into a bag station where the user applies a label, zips up the bag and places it ona takeaway belt.”

steps.title: Compare the two flows using only the source-described differences
steps.purpose: Ensure the explanation clearly contrasts operator-driven destination handling (traditional) versus conveyor “slug” bin-drop movement to a bag station (belted).
steps.instruction: Using the source segment, compare traditional vs belted ACB using only the described differences: traditional relies on operator actions at the destination (close/print/apply/zip/reopen), while belted ACB uses a dropped bin and conveyor “slug” movement to a bag station.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately state the contrast: traditional = operator closes destination/prints/applies label/zips/reopens chute; belted = destination full triggers bin drop to takeaway conveyor conveying packages as a slug down a chute into a bag station.
steps.healthy_condition: Your comparison includes both sides’ named mechanisms and does not mix steps between models.
steps.failure_condition: Your comparison blends the two models (e.g., adding traditional destination close/reopen chute to belted, or replacing belted slug/bin-drop with traditional chute/bag operator close).

actions.label: Restate model differences
actions.exact_action: Restate the contrast using the source’s named elements: traditional operator closes destination/prints/apply label/zips/reopens chute vs belted destination full → bin dropped on takeaway conveyor as a slug → chute → bag station.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot map the described steps to the correct model (traditional vs belted), stop and re-check the source wording for the named elements (destination, chute, bag, label, zips, takeaway belt/conveyor, bin dropped, slug, bag station).

source_evidence.quote_or_evidence: Traditional: “...operator closes the destination, prints a label, applies the label to the bag, zips up the bag, places the bag on a takeaway belt, and then reopens the chute.” Belted: “...when a destination is full the bin is dropped on a takeaway conveyor that conveys the packages as a slug that go down a chute into a bag station...”

success_criteria: User can accurately restate the source-described parcel-to-bag-to-takeaway flow for both models (traditional and belted ACB), including the named actions (close destination/print/apply/zip/reopen vs bin dropped to takeaway conveyor as a slug to chute/bag station).
healthy_conditions: Traditional explanation includes: operators assigned sections of destinations (20-25) → parcels divert down destination into a bag → when bag full: close destination, print label, apply label, zip bag, place on takeaway belt, reopen chute.
Belted explanation includes: destination full → bin dropped on takeaway conveyor → packages conveyed as a slug down a chute into a bag station → user applies label, zips bag, places on takeaway belt.
Comparison does not mix traditional destination close/reopen chute steps into belted, and does not replace belted slug/bin-drop mechanism with traditional operator destination handling.
failure_conditions: User cannot correctly map steps to the correct model (traditional vs belted).
User omits one or more named elements in either flow (destination/shoot, bag, label, zips, takeaway belt, chute reopening; or belted bin-drop, slug, chute, bag station).
User blends the two models’ sequences (mixing operator destination close/reopen chute with belted slug/bin-drop).
escalation_guidance: If the user cannot map the described steps to the correct model, stop and re-check the source wording for the named elements: destination, chute, bag, label, zips, takeaway belt/conveyor, bin dropped, slug, bag station.
